newsitem.title: USA: Northwestern Steel Q1 hurt by low orders.
newsitem.headline: Northwestern Steel Q1 hurt by low orders.

text.p: Northwestern Steel & Wire Co, reporting a loss for the October 31 first quarter, said earnings were hurt by reduced orders.
"These reductions were directly related to uncertainties surrounding labor negotiations, which were successfully concluded on July 31, 1996," said chairman Robert Gurnitz in a statement.
Gurnitz said volumes through the company's medium and heavy structural rolling mills, which generally account for about 50 percent of its business, were down sharply in the quarter.
As the quarter came to a close, operations were profitable, Gurnitz noted.

"Product mix has improved and shipments of value-added finished products are expected to be a greater percentage of volume in the months ahead," Gurnitz said. "We also expect improved profitability in our large and medium structural business. Our businsses are poised to reach market share levels which were achieved prior to the labor-related falloff."

Northwestern Steel, a producer of structural steel components, posted a quarterly loss of $0.08 per share compared to a year-ago profit of $0.19 per share. Sales declined to $145.2 million from $160.9 million.
